Using edger.bp

Source: vignettes/usage.Rmd
usage.Rmd

edger.bp runs edgeR-compatible analyses on genes-by-samples count matrices stored with BPCells. It is intended for pseudobulk matrices where the number of genes is large enough that row-blocked GLM fitting and file-backed storage are useful.

The package does not define new statistical methods. It mirrors supported edgeR workflows for BPCells-backed matrices, so statistical choices should follow the edgeR documentation.

Data Contract

Inputs should satisfy the usual edgeR count-matrix requirements:

  • rows are genes or features;
  • columns are samples or pseudobulk sample-cluster columns;
  • entries are non-negative integer counts;
  • row names and column names are present and unique;
  • nrow(design) equals the number of matrix columns;
  • optional group values are aligned to the matrix columns.

For large analyses, create the BPCells matrix before calling edger.bp. Keep a column metadata table alongside it with any sample, cluster, batch, or donor fields needed to build design matrices.

A Small Runnable Example

The example below simulates a small two-group pseudobulk experiment and writes the counts to a temporary BPCells directory.

library(edger.bp)
library(BPCells)
library(Matrix)

set.seed(7)

ngenes <- 120L
nsamples <- 8L
group <- factor(rep(c("ctrl", "stim"), each = 4L))

base_mean <- rgamma(ngenes, shape = 2, rate = 0.15)
fold_change <- rep(1, ngenes)
fold_change[seq_len(12L)] <- 2.5

counts <- vapply(seq_len(nsamples), function(j) {
    mu <- base_mean * ifelse(group[[j]] == "stim", fold_change, 1)
    as.integer(rnbinom(ngenes, mu = mu, size = 8))
}, integer(ngenes))

rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(ngenes))
colnames(counts) <- paste0("sample", seq_len(nsamples))

bp_dir <- tempfile("edger-bp-counts-")
sparse_counts <- Matrix(counts, sparse = TRUE)
sparse_counts <- BPCells::convert_matrix_type(sparse_counts, "uint32_t")
bp_counts <- BPCells::write_matrix_dir(sparse_counts, dir = bp_dir)

design <- model.matrix(~ group)
colnames(design)
#> [1] "(Intercept)" "groupstim"

The audited package versions can be checked explicitly:

bp_check_versions(error = FALSE)
#>   package installed expected version_supported   ok     stack
#> 1       R     4.5.3    4.5.3              TRUE TRUE conda-r45
#> 2   edgeR     4.8.2    4.8.2              TRUE TRUE conda-r45
#> 3   limma    3.66.0   3.66.0              TRUE TRUE conda-r45
#> 4 BPCells     0.3.1    0.3.1              TRUE TRUE conda-r45

Likelihood-Ratio Test

bp_lrt() runs preparation, optional filtering, TMM normalization, dispersion estimation, and blockwise GLM LRT testing. The returned object keeps those stages separate.

lrt_fit <- bp_lrt(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    dispersion.method = "stream",
    block.size = 50L,
    workers = 1L
)

names(lrt_fit)
#> [1] "prepare"    "dispersion" "lrt"
head(lrt_fit$lrt$table[order(lrt_fit$lrt$table$PValue), ])
#>             logFC   logCPM        LR      PValue
#> gene50 -1.3440732 13.14280 10.087414 0.001492854
#> gene75  1.2826286 13.48391  8.719293 0.003148602
#> gene86  0.9841068 13.39220  5.240966 0.022061027
#> gene49 -0.9028414 13.35884  4.728981 0.029658459
#> gene29  0.8451257 13.37477  3.901494 0.048243195
#> gene45  0.7526657 13.49282  3.164025 0.075277385

Important components are:

  • prepare: filtered counts, library sizes, normalization factors, and offsets;
  • dispersion: common, trended, and tagwise dispersion estimates;
  • lrt$table: the edgeR-style result table for the requested coefficient or contrast.

QL F-Test and Treat

bp_qlf() and bp_treat() use edgeR’s modern quasi-likelihood path by default. They can also accept a supplied scalar or gene-level dispersion vector when that matches the intended edgeR analysis.

qlf_fit <- bp_qlf(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    dispersion.method = "stream",
    block.size = 50L,
    workers = 1L
)

head(qlf_fit$qlf$table[order(qlf_fit$qlf$table$PValue), ])
#>             logFC   logCPM        F      PValue
#> gene50 -1.3439926 13.14280 9.692360 0.001932632
#> gene75  1.2827450 13.48391 8.211283 0.004299308
#> gene86  0.9840272 13.39220 4.971189 0.026118029
#> gene49 -0.9028356 13.35884 4.499580 0.034285776
#> gene29  0.8453132 13.37477 3.701896 0.054792438
#> gene45  0.7526489 13.49282 2.979832 0.084789141

bp_treat() tests whether the effect exceeds a log2 fold-change threshold. The default threshold follows edgeR’s glmTreat() default, log2(1.2).

treat_fit <- bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    dispersion.method = "stream",
    lfc = log2(1.2),
    block.size = 50L,
    workers = 1L
)

head(treat_fit$treat$table[order(treat_fit$treat$table$PValue), ])
#>             logFC unshrunk.logFC   logCPM      PValue
#> gene50 -1.3439926     -1.3512817 13.14280 0.003282173
#> gene75  1.2827450      1.2885989 13.48391 0.006672171
#> gene86  0.9840272      0.9885210 13.39220 0.035175862
#> gene49 -0.9028356     -0.9067826 13.35884 0.045901236
#> gene29  0.8453132      0.8491799 13.37477 0.069344274
#> gene39  0.8594424      0.8693028 12.20338 0.100362196

For legacy edgeR quasi-likelihood comparisons, use qlf.args or treat.args:

bp_qlf(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    qlf.args = list(legacy = TRUE)
)

bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    treat.args = list(legacy = TRUE)
)

One-vs-Rest Marker Tests

A common marker workflow builds one binary design per cluster. The pseudobulk matrix still has genes as rows and pseudobulk columns as samples; only the design changes.

cluster <- col_data$cluster
selected <- cluster == "cl01"
design_marker <- model.matrix(~ selected)

marker_cl01 <- bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design_marker,
    group = selected,
    coef = "selectedTRUE",
    lfc = log2(1.2),
    block.size = 1000L,
    workers = 4L
)

marker_table <- marker_cl01$treat$table

This binary one-vs-rest design directly compares the selected cluster to all other columns pooled together. A shared ~ 0 + cluster design with contrasts can be faster for many clusters, but it is a different estimand and should be chosen deliberately.

Storage Order and Parallelism

BPCells matrices have a physical storage order. Column-ordered storage is useful for sample-wise operations such as library sizes and TMM normalization. Row- ordered storage is useful for blockwise gene operations. If you need a companion matrix with the other storage order, use bp_ensure_storage_order().

bp_counts_row <- bp_ensure_storage_order(
    bp_counts,
    order = "row",
    outdir = "cache/counts_row",
    tmpdir = "cache/tmp"
)

The main tuning arguments are:

  • block.size: number of genes materialized per edgeR block;
  • workers: number of row blocks processed in parallel where supported;
  • Slurm resources: for full datasets, run package workflows in batch jobs and budget memory as roughly proportional to workers * block.size * ncol(y).

Small interactive checks should use workers = 1L or 2L. Full pseudobulk marker runs should use Slurm and an explicit wall-time/QoS choice appropriate to the cluster.

Full-Scale Workflow

A typical full-scale analysis is:

  1. Build or load a genes-by-pseudobulk BPCells count matrix.
  2. Load column metadata and construct the design matrix.
  3. Run a small smoke test on a subset of genes or clusters.
  4. Run the full workflow with recorded block.size, workers, package versions, and Slurm resources.
  5. Save the result table plus enough metadata to reproduce the design and contrast.

For example:

bp_counts <- BPCells::open_matrix_dir("cache/counts_col")
col_data <- read.delim("cache/sample_metadata.tsv")

group <- factor(col_data$condition)
design <- model.matrix(~ group)

fit <- bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "grouptreated",
    block.size = 1000L,
    workers = 8L
)

write.table(
    fit$treat$table,
    file = "results/edgeR_treat.tsv",
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    col.names = NA
)
